Fake support and account takeover on Telegram and WhatsApp

Many thefts start with a private message that looks like official help. A few habits are enough to stop most of these tricks.

How the trick works

  • You ask a question in a public group or on X. Within minutes a “support agent” writes to you privately. Real support almost never starts a chat with you.
  • The agent sends a link to “verify your wallet”, “sync it” or “fix an error”. The page asks for your seed phrase or tricks you into signing a harmful approval.
  • Another version: a friend's account, already hijacked, asks you for a quick loan or to “vote” through a link.
  • Another version: you receive a login code you did not request, and a stranger asks you to read it out “by mistake”. That code lets them into your account.
  • Admins or moderators with the same name and photo as the real ones are copies. Always check the exact username.

Lock down your accounts

  1. Turn on two-step verification in Telegram. Settings, Privacy and Security, Two-Step Verification. Set a password only you know.
  2. Do the same in WhatsApp. Settings, Account, Two-step verification, and add a recovery email.
  3. Never share a login code. Not with support, not with a friend, not with anyone. A code only goes into the app you are logging in to.
  4. Check your active sessions. In Telegram open Settings, Devices. In WhatsApp open Linked devices. Remove any you do not recognise.
  5. Limit who can add you to groups in the privacy settings, so strangers cannot pull you into scam chats.

Rules for dealing with “support”

  • Contact support only through the official website or the help section inside the app. Type the address yourself.
  • Ignore private messages that offer help. Block and report them.
  • Never give a seed phrase, private key, password or login code. No real company needs them.
  • If a friend asks for money by message, call them or ask a question only they can answer before you send anything.
  • Do not install apps or screen-sharing tools because a stranger asks you to.

If your account or wallet was hit

  • Log out all other sessions and change your passwords. In Telegram: Settings, Devices, Terminate all other sessions.
  • Tell your contacts and groups at once, so they ignore messages sent from your account.
  • If you shared a seed phrase or key, create a new wallet on a clean device and move what remains. Revoke old approvals.
  • Report it to the platform and to your local police or cybercrime unit. Keep screenshots, usernames and transaction IDs.
  • Be careful with “recovery services” that ask for a fee. This is a very common second scam.

Tools mentioned in this guide

  • GoPlus Security

    Checks tokens, contracts and links for common scam and honeypot risks.

    How to start (5 steps)
    1. Open the GoPlus website and find its token security checker.
    2. Choose the blockchain network the token lives on, such as Ethereum, BNB Chain, Solana or TRON.
    3. Paste the contract address. Copy it from the project's official website or from CoinGecko, not from a chat message, then run the check.
    4. Read the warnings first: honeypot (you can buy but not sell), very high buy or sell tax, an owner who can mint new tokens or change the rules, and hidden owners.
    5. If the report shows several risks, do not buy or approve anything. If it looks clean, remember that is only one input.

    A clean scan is not a guarantee. New scams are built to pass checks, and the tool cannot see the team's plans.

    Level: Beginner
